questions.stem: Which of the following statements is false regarding accommodative esotropia?

options.label: A
options.text: It is the most common type of squint

options.label: B
options.text: Miotics are used as the treatment strategy in the high AC/A ratio

options.label: C
options.text: It is associated with high myopia.

options.label: D
options.text: Refractive type can be fully corrected by the use of spectacles

questions.answerText: It is associated with high myopia.
questions.solutionHtml:
It is associated with high myopia.
  • Accommodative esotropia is one of the most common types of strabismus in childhood. The incidence is estimated at 2% of the population. It is usually found in patients with moderate amounts of hyperopia.
  • As the patient accommodates or focuses the eyes, the eyes converge. The over-convergence associated with the accommodation to overcome a hyperopic refractive error can cause a loss of binocular control and lead to the development of esotropia
  • Spectacle correction is the initial treatment for accommodative esotropia. Generally, the full cycloplegic correction should be given initially.


Parsons Disease of the Eye, 23rd Edition, Page No. 368, 377

questions.stem: A 3-year-old child presents with a right convergent squint of 6 months duration. What is the appropriate management?

options.label: A
options.text: Immediate surgical correction followed by amblyopia therapy

options.label: B
options.text: Proper refractive correction, amblyopia therapy followed by surgical correction

options.label: C
options.text: Prescribe spectacles and defer surgery until the child is 5-year-old

options.label: D
options.text: Botulinum toxin injection followed by occlusion therapy

questions.answerText: Proper refractive correction, amblyopia therapy followed by surgical correction
questions.solutionHtml:
Proper refractive correction, amblyopia therapy followed by surgical correction
  • Uncorrected long sight (hypermetropia) is the most common reason for a convergent squint. Vision will be blurred and the effort required to see more clearly can cause one eye to turn inwards.
  • Spectacle correction is the initial treatment for accommodative esotropia. Generally, the full cycloplegic correction should be given initially.


Parson’s Disease of the Eye, 23rd Edition, Page No.377

questions.stem: A person having limitation of adduction in the left eye. In the right eye saccadic movement on abduction and normal convergence. What is the most probable diagnosis?
questions.solutionHtml:
Internuclear Ophthalmoplegia
  • Internuclear ophthalmoplegia (INO) is a disorder of conjugate lateral gaze in which the affected eye shows impairment of adduction. When an attempt is made to gaze contra laterally (relative to the affected eye), the affected eye adducts minimally, if at all.
  • The contralateral eye abducts, however, with nystagmus. Additionally, the divergence of the eyes leads to horizontal diplopia. That is, if the right eye is affected the patient will "see double" when looking to the left, seeing two images side-by-side. Convergence is generally preserved


Parson’s Disease of the Eye, 23rd Edition, Page No. 418

questions.stem: Superior oblique testing for the 4th nerve is done by checking its intorsion while asking the subject to look-
questions.solutionHtml:
Down and in
  • The Superior oblique muscle can be tested by requesting the patient to adduct the eye and then asking to depress the eye. Failure to depress the eye during adduction indicates a problem with the superior oblique muscle or the trochlear nerve.



Parson’s Disease of the Eye, 23rd Edition, Page No. 416

questions.stem: The yoke muscle of the right superior oblique is?
questions.solutionHtml:
Left inferior rectus

The muscles that move the eye are called the extraocular muscles. There are six of them on each eye. They work together in pairs—complementary (or yoke) muscles pulling the eyes in the same direction(s), and opposites (or antagonists) pulling the eyes in opposite directions.




Parson’s Disease of the Eye, 23rd Edition, Page No. 404

questions.stem: 66 years old diabetic patient came to OPD. On examination, it was found that primary deviation is lesser than secondary deviation. The forced duction test was found to be negative. Which of the following types of squint is most likely to be present in this patient?
questions.solutionHtml:
Paralytic squint

In the given scenario, the secondary deviation is more than the primary deviation which is suggestive of incomitant squint. To differentiate between paralytic and restrictive squint, a forced duction test is performed, which in the patient is negative.



Comprehensive Ophthalmology by A K Khurana, 7th EditionPage No. 354

questions.stemHtml: The pattern of esotropia shown in a given image is:
questions.solutionHtml:
V pattern esotropia
  • The terms 'A' or 'V' pattern squint are labelled when the amount of deviation in the squinting eye varies by more than 10° and 15°, respectively, between upward and downward gaze.
  • a ‘V’ pattern is seen in a convergent squint which increases on a downward gaze


Comprehensive Ophthalmology by A K Khurana, 7th Edition Page No. 356

questions.stem: Recession & Resection surgeries are based on which mechanism of EOM movements?

options.label: B
options.text: Length & arc of contact of muscle

questions.answerText: Length & arc of contact of muscle
questions.solutionHtml:
Length & arc of contact of muscle
  • The power of a muscle is proportional to its length & arc of contact. Retroplacement of the insertion of muscle ( recession) weakens the action of muscle by shortening its effective length & by reducing its arc of contact in various positions of gaze.
  • Advancements in the EOM have a strengthening effect because of the increase in the effective length & arc of contact of the muscle.




Parson’s Disease of the Eye, 23rd Edition, Page No. 355
